newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN agencies pledge more than $350,000 to Iran.
newsitem.headline: UN agencies pledge more than $350,000 to Iran.

text.p: U.N. agencies have pledged $360,000 to Iran's earthquake victims, beginning with a $50,000 cash grant from the Department of Humanitarian Affairs, a U.N. spokesman said on Monday.
The U.N. Development Programme has pledged $200,000 and the U.N. Children's Fund UNICEF $100,000. The World Health Organisation is expected to contribute an initial $10,000.
A huge earthquake on Saturday killed at least 2,400 people and injured as many as 6,000. Homes, health clinics and other structures crumbled in villages hit hardest.
Iran has appealed for emergency supplies through the United Nations, and the Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies appealed separately for $8.2 million.

According to a U.N. list, Japan was contributing $280,000 worth of supplies, including tents, blankets and torch lights directly to Iran and Britain has contributed about $160,000 through the Red Cross to puchase supplies locally.

Switzerland has sent an advance rescue team, France has sent 40 metric tons of emergency items and a 30-member rescue squad backed by sniffer dogs, and Russia is sending two aircraft loaded with relief items, it said.
Several other countries have announced separately that they are sending relief supplies.
